previous_action: Gaius Maximus Valerius turns the extremely narrow ravine into a fortress connected to his main estate and publicly declares it his property, using it as a forward operating base. He does not slow the expedition or give reckless chase. Instead he scouts deliberately, sends men to identify other likely ambush sites, and prepares counter-ambushes against the regional band.

continuity.campaign_development: In June 60 BCE, Valerius converted the narrow ravine used by the regional band into a permanent fortified forward station publicly declared as his property and linked to his principal estate. He continued operations rather than retreating, sending scouts to identify likely ambush grounds and preparing counter-ambush positions. A small bandit scouting party was caught and driven away near one of the prepared approaches. The main force remains in the field and the regional band remains active.
